rm(list = ls()) # clear the environment
# Load the shapefile with BBS routes

                    xmax = -60,

2.8 Human footprint and its temporal change (1993-2009)

footprint93 <- terra::rast("rasters/footprint93.tif")
footprint09 <- terra::rast("rasters/footprint09.tif")
delta.footprint <- footprint09 - footprint93

# extract the values from the rasters to routes
routes$footprint93 <- terra::extract(footprint93, routes, fun = mean)[,2]
routes$footprint09 <- terra::extract(footprint09, routes, fun = mean)[,2]
routes$footprint93to09 <- terra::extract(delta.footprint, routes, fun = mean)[,2]

2.9 Human population density in 2000

# load the 2.5 min raster with human population density
pop2000 <- log10(rast("rasters/pop2000.tif") + 1)

# extract the population density values, summing the values of 2.5 min pixels touching a route
routes$pop2000 <- terra::extract(pop2000, routes, fun = mean)[,2]

list.files("pesticides_data/", full.names = T)

}

pesticide_2013_2017 <- read_delim("pesticides_data/per_county_2013_2017/EPest_county_estimates_2013_2017_v2.txt",
                                  delim = "\t", escape_double = FALSE,
                                  trim_ws = TRUE)
for(y in c(2013:2017)){
  assign(paste0("pesticide_",y),
         pesticide_2013_2017[pesticide_2013_2017$YEAR == y,])
}

rm(pesticide_2013_2017)

pesticide_2018 <- read_delim("pesticides_data/per_county_2018/EPest_county_estimates_2018.txt",
                             delim = "\t", escape_double = FALSE,
                             trim_ws = TRUE)
## Filter the pesticides that are reported every year from 1992 to 2018
compounds <- c()
# Get all the compounds present from 1992 to 2018
for(d in ls()[grepl("pesticide_", ls())]){
  compounds <- append(compounds, unique(get(d)$COMPOUND))
}
compounds <- unique(compounds)
# Get the list of the ones reported every year
for(d in ls()[grepl("pesticide_", ls())]){
  compounds <- unique(get(d)$COMPOUND)[unique(get(d)$COMPOUND) %in% compounds]
}

2.10.1 Average pesticide

shp <- readRDS("shapefile_counties/sites_counties.RDS")
shp_area <- readRDS("shapefile_counties/area_counties.RDS")
# Compute the log(sum all pesticides/county area)
for(d in ls()[grepl("pesticide_", ls())]){
  assign(print(d),
         get(d) %>%
           filter(COMPOUND %in% compounds) %>%
           unite(state_county, STATE_FIPS_CODE, COUNTY_FIPS_CODE, sep = "_") %>%
           group_by(YEAR, state_county) %>%
           summarise(EPEST_LOW_KG = sum(EPEST_LOW_KG, na.rm = T),
                     EPEST_HIGH_KG = sum(EPEST_HIGH_KG, na.rm = T)) %>%
           ungroup() %>% 
           left_join(shp, by = "state_county") %>%
           left_join(shp_area, by = "state_county") %>% 
           mutate(pesticide_low = log(EPEST_LOW_KG/as.numeric(area_m_2)),
                  pesticide_high = log(EPEST_HIGH_KG/as.numeric(area_m_2))) 
         )
}
## Merge all the pesticide data together
all_pesticide <- pesticide_1992[0,]
for(d in ls()[grepl("pesticide_", ls())]){
  all_pesticide <- rbind(all_pesticide, get(d))
}
## Group by county and get the mean log(sum all pesticides/county area)
mean_pesticide <- all_pesticide %>% 
  group_by(state_county) %>% 
  summarise(mean_pesticide_low = mean(pesticide_low),
            mean_pesticide_high = mean(pesticide_high)) %>% 
  ungroup()

## Merge with shapefile
mean_pesticide <- mean_pesticide %>% 
  left_join(shp, by = "state_county") %>%
  left_join(shp_area, by = "state_county") %>%
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "geometry") %>% 
  st_transform(st_crs(routes))

# Extract max of the pesticide value across all counties each route touches
routes$mean_pesticide <- sapply(
  sf::st_intersects(routes, mean_pesticide),
  function(i) if (length(i)) max(mean_pesticide$mean_pesticide_high[i], na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
)

2.10.2 Pesticide use trend (1992-2018)

## Assess the change in pesticide use using lm
# There is only one -Inf value for log(pesticide/m^2) in 2017, replace with NA
all_pesticide$pesticide_high[!is.finite(all_pesticide$pesticide_high)] <- NA

## Perform the lm between log(pesticide/county area) and time
trend_pesticide <-
  all_pesticide %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  group_by(state_county) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  do({
    fit <- lm(pesticide_high ~ YEAR, data = .)
    tibble(
      slope_per_year = coef(fit)[2]
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

## Merge with the shapefile
trend_pesticide <-
  trend_pesticide %>% 
  left_join(shp, by = "state_county") %>%
  left_join(shp_area, by = "state_county") %>% 
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "geometry") %>% 
  st_transform(st_crs(routes))

# Extract max of the pesticide value across all counties each route touches
routes$pesticide_change <- sapply(
  sf::st_intersects(routes, trend_pesticide),
  function(i) if (length(i)) max(trend_pesticide$slope_per_year[i], na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
)

4 Load the estimated demographic rates

# Load the models' output
for(file in list.files("../mixed_model/outputs/", full.names = T)){
  assign(gsub("^../mixed_model/outputs/|\\.rds$","",file),
         readRDS(file = file))
}

# THE GAM MODEL 
# extract latitude and longitude of route centroids
coords <- data.frame(st_centroid(routes) %>% st_coordinates() )
## Warning: st_centroid assumes attributes are constant over geometries
names(coords) <- c("lon","lat")
routes <- cbind(routes, coords)

## Add raw (not smoothed) values the dataset
routes$delta_N <- as.numeric(overall_N_output$mean$beta1)
routes$delta_g <- as.numeric(overall_g_output$mean$beta1)
routes$delta_absg <- as.numeric(overall_absg_output$mean$beta1)

# fit the gam models
routes$delta_N_gam <- gam(delta_N ~ s(lon, lat, bs = "gp", k = 100, m = 2),
                          data = routes)$fitted.values
routes$delta_g_gam <- gam(delta_g ~ s(lon, lat, bs = "gp", k = 100, m = 2),
                          data = routes)$fitted.values
routes$delta_absg_gam <- gam(delta_absg ~ s(lon, lat, bs = "gp", k = 100, m = 2),
                          data = routes)$fitted.values

# prepare data.frame for analyses
# data.frame(names(routes))
dat <- as.data.frame(routes[, 24:ncol(routes)])

# remove variables that we don't want in the pairplot
dat <- select(dat, -c("geometry")) # remove the last "geometry" column
dat <- select(dat, -c("crops19", "footprint09")) 
dat <- select(dat, -c("lat", "lon")) # remove spatial coordinates

6 Tree-based analysis

6.1 Smoothed values

Set predictors

# set all the predictors here which will be used in all the rf models
rf.predictors <- c("grass",
                   "trees",
                   "shrubs",
                   "water",
                   "temp",
                   "Nfertilizer",
                   # "mean_pesticide",
                   "pesticide_change",
                   # "crops03",
                   "footprint93",
                   "NDVI82to12",
                   "temp87to21",
                   "footprint93to09",
                   "crops03to19")

6.1.1 Absolute growth rate change (delta absg)

# First we split the dataset into training and validation datasets
set.seed(333)
traindata <- trainControl(method = "repeatedcv", number = 10, repeats = 3)

# Impute missing data for pesticide change in Canada and Alaska
imputed_data <- missForest::missForest(dat[, c(rf.predictors, "delta_absg_gam")])$ximp

## We use three tree-based algorithms in order to assess which one perform the best
## Create the list of models
model_list_deltaabsg <-
  caretList(
    delta_absg_gam ~ ., 
    data = imputed_data,
    trControl = traindata,
    metric = "RMSE",
    tuneList = list(
      rf =  caretModelSpec(method = "ranger", 
                           importance = "permutation",
                           tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = ceiling((ncol(dat[,rf.predictors])-1)/3),
                                                                    splitrule = "variance",
                                                                    min.node.size = 5)),
      gbm = caretModelSpec(method = "gbm",
                           distribution = "gaussian",
                           # keep.data = TRUE,
                           tuneGrid = data.frame(n.trees = 500,
                                                 interaction.depth = 1,
                                                 shrinkage = 0.1,
                                                 n.minobsinnode = 5)),
      xgboost = caretModelSpec(method = "xgbTree",
                               tuneGrid = expand.grid(nrounds = 500,
                                                     max_depth = 5,
                                                     eta = 0.1,
                                                     gamma = 0,
                                                     colsample_bytree = 1,
                                                     min_child_weight = 1,
                                                     subsample = 1))
    )
  )

# saveRDS(model_list_deltaabsg, "models/model_list_deltaabsg.rds")

6.1.4 Assess the best models

## For delta N
resamples_deltaN <- resamples(model_list_deltaN)
summary(resamples_deltaN)
## 
## Call:
## summary.resamples(object = resamples_deltaN)
## 
## Models: rf, gbm, xgboost 
## Number of resamples: 30 
## 
## MAE 
##              Min.   1st Qu.    Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. NA's
## rf      0.9485630 1.1233960 1.1515154 1.175397 1.268879 1.340538    0
## gbm     1.3615736 1.5774349 1.6447868 1.652270 1.725517 1.912682    0
## xgboost 0.8438443 0.9405851 0.9993149 1.011767 1.101506 1.193773    0
## 
## RMSE 
##             Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. NA's
## rf      1.232264 1.380186 1.513409 1.504032 1.622622 1.777688    0
## gbm     1.673358 1.966637 2.030300 2.042301 2.130268 2.316952    0
## xgboost 1.062658 1.214954 1.302082 1.335050 1.433368 1.602891    0
## 
## Rsquared 
##              Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max. NA's

6.2 Raw values

6.2.1 Absolute growth rate change (delta absg)

# First we split the dataset into training and validation datasets
set.seed(333)
traindata <- trainControl(method = "repeatedcv", number = 10, repeats = 3)

# Impute missing data for pesticide change in Canada
imputed_data <- missForest::missForest(dat[, c(rf.predictors, "delta_absg")])$ximp

## We use three tree-based algorithms in order to assess which one perform the best
## Create the list of models
model_list_deltaabsg_raw <-
  caretList(
    delta_absg ~ ., 
    data = imputed_data,
    trControl = traindata,
    metric = "RMSE",
    tuneList = list(
      rf =  caretModelSpec(method = "ranger", 
                           importance = "permutation",
                           tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = ceiling((ncol(dat[,rf.predictors])-1)/3),
                                                                    splitrule = "variance",
                                                                    min.node.size = 5)),
      gbm = caretModelSpec(method = "gbm",
                           distribution = "gaussian",
                           # keep.data = TRUE,
                           tuneGrid = data.frame(n.trees = 500,
                                                 interaction.depth = 1,
                                                 shrinkage = 0.1,
                                                 n.minobsinnode = 5)),
      xgboost = caretModelSpec(method = "xgbTree",
                               tuneGrid = expand.grid(nrounds = 500,
                                                     max_depth = 5,
                                                     eta = 0.1,
                                                     gamma = 0,
                                                     colsample_bytree = 1,
                                                     min_child_weight = 1,
                                                     subsample = 1))
    )
  )

# saveRDS(model_list_deltaabsg_raw, "models/model_list_deltaabsg_raw.rds")

6.2.3 Abundance change (delta N)

# Impute missing data for pesticide change in Canada
imputed_data <- missForest::missForest(dat[, c(rf.predictors, "delta_N")])$ximp

## Create the list of models
model_list_deltaN_raw <-
  caretList(
    delta_N ~ .,
    data = imputed_data,
    trControl = traindata,
    metric = "RMSE",
    tuneList = list(
      rf =  caretModelSpec(method = "ranger", 
                           importance = "permutation",
                           tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = ceiling((ncol(dat[,rf.predictors])-1)/3),
                                                                    splitrule = "variance",
                                                                    min.node.size = 5)),
      gbm = caretModelSpec(method = "gbm",
                           distribution = "gaussian",
                           # keep.data = TRUE,
                           tuneGrid = data.frame(n.trees = 500,
                                                 interaction.depth = 1,
                                                 shrinkage = 0.1,
                                                 n.minobsinnode = 5)),
      xgboost = caretModelSpec(method = "xgbTree",
                               tuneGrid = expand.grid(nrounds = 500,
                                                     max_depth = 5,
                                                     eta = 0.1,
                                                     gamma = 0,
                                                     colsample_bytree = 1,
                                                     min_child_weight = 1,
                                                     subsample = 1))
    )
  )

# saveRDS(model_list_deltaN_raw, "models/model_list_deltaN_raw.rds")

6.2.4 Plot Variable importances

# Using the same algorithms than for the smoothed values (i.e. XGBoost for delta N, delta abs g and RF for delta g)
pdf("importance_deltaN_raw.pdf", width = 5.83, height = 4.13)

varImp(model_list_deltaN_raw$xgboost)$importance %>% 
  mutate(Overall = (Overall*model_list_deltaN_raw$xgboost$results$Rsquared/sum(Overall))*100) %>% 
  mutate(response = "deltaN") %>% 
  rownames_to_column() %>% 
  rename(variable = "rowname",
         importance = "Overall") %>% 
  mutate(variable = case_when(
    variable == "temp" ~ "Mean Temperature\n(1970-2000)",
    variable == "temp87to21" ~ "Temperature change\n(1987-2021)",
    variable == "trees" ~ "Tree cover\n(2020)",
    variable == "shrubs" ~ "Shrub cover\n(2020)",
    variable == "Nfertilizer" ~ "Nitrogen fertilizer use\n(1994-2001)",
    # variable == "mean_pesticide" ~ "Mean Pesticide",
    variable == "pesticide_change" ~ "Pesticide change\n(1992-2018)",
    variable == "footprint93to09" ~ "Human foortprint change\n(1993-2009)",
    variable == "grass" ~ "Grassland cover\n(2020)",
    variable == "footprint93" ~ "Human footprint\n(1993)",
    variable == "crops03to19" ~ "Crops cover change\n(2003-2019)",
    variable == "NDVI82to12" ~ "NDVI change\n(1982-2012)",
    variable == "water" ~ "Water cover\n(2020)")) %>% 
  mutate(variable = reorder(variable, importance)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = importance, y = variable, fill = variable)) +
  geom_col() +
  xlab("Relative importance")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = covariate_colors, guide = "none")+
  theme_bw()

6.2.5.1 Growth rate change (delta g)

covariate_labels <- c(
  "temp" = "Mean Temperature\n(1970-2000)",
  "temp87to21" = "Temperature change\n(1987-2021)",
  "trees" = "Tree cover\n(2020)",
  "shrubs" = "Shrub cover\n(2020)",
  "Nfertilizer" = "Nitrogen fertilizer use\n(1994-2001)",
  # "mean_pesticide" = "Mean Pesticide",
  "pesticide_change" = "Pesticide change\n(1992-2018)",
  # "crops03" = "Cropland area\n(2003)",
  "footprint93to09" = "Human foortprint change\n(1993-2009)",
  "grass" = "Grassland cover\n(2020)",
  "footprint93" = "Human footprint\n(1993)",
  "crops03to19" = "Crops cover change\n(2003-2019)",
  "NDVI82to12" = "NDVI change\n(1982-2012)",
  "water" = "Water cover\n(2020)"
)

pp <- data.frame(x = as.numeric(), y = as.numeric(), covariate = as.character())
for(cov in model_list_deltaN$xgboost$coefnames){
  
  pp <- rbind(pp, 
              partial(model_list_deltag_raw$rf, cov,
                      train = dat[,c(rf.predictors,"delta_g_gam")]) %>%
                mutate(covariate = cov) %>% rename(x = cov))
  
}

# Rename covariate column
pp$covariate <- covariate_labels[pp$covariate]
# Reorder
pp$covariate <- factor(pp$covariate, levels = importance_order_deltag_raw)


pdf("pdp_g_raw.pdf", width = 8.27, height = 5.83)

ggplot(pp)+
  geom_line(aes(x, yhat, color = covariate), size = 1)+
  facet_wrap(vars(covariate), scales = "free_x", drop = F)+
  ylab("Growth rate change (delta g)")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 7.3),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 6),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  )+
  scale_color_manual(values = covariate_colors, guide = "none")+
  annotate("segment", x=-Inf, xend=Inf, y=-Inf, yend=-Inf, size = .7)+
  annotate("segment", x=-Inf, xend=-Inf, y=-Inf, yend=Inf, size = .7)
